## 7bba59d92716

### Reproduced shortcut coverage hole inside the accepted input domain

The intended authority recolors the middle of qualifying length-five vertical connected components. A rival instead recolors the middle of every maximal length-five vertical run, ignoring attached same-colored branches. It fits all four training examples and agrees with Racket on 60/60 default draws, because ordinary generation makes separated vertical lines without attached arms.

Exact witness: an 8×10 zero grid; set color 1 in rows 1..5 at both columns 2 and 7, then add a color-1 cell at `(3,3)`. The left structure is now a six-cell branched component; the right structure remains an isolated five-cell vertical component. Racket changes only `(3,7)` to 2. The run-only rival additionally changes `(3,2)` to 2. The generator's own self-check returns no errors on this witness, so this is a gap within its accepted input domain rather than only a rejected extension. The generator never samples the distinguishing branch because it constructs isolated, separated columns.

The discrepancy is Racket-confirmed. That a learner will actually adopt this shortcut remains an unmeasured hypothesis. Add at least one ordinary branch-connected decoy and preserve a qualifying isolated target in teaching windows; check the full component-based rule rather than inferring it from column length alone.

### Reproduced override defects

`generate(0,0,n_lines=1,palette_size=1)` is byte-identical to the default: it still has two qualifying length-five lines and nonzero palette `{1,6}`. An invented override key is accepted and also returns the default. These are exact ignored-control reproductions, not statistical differences. Validate accepted names and enforce or reject requested values.

Source reviewed: SHA256 `83027286f56bc25d40f4f748e1e46e7bc70beaf24fe9fad1d4fdad6ad4e12cab`. Neither this repair nor any approval change is included in the assigned-task patch.

## 7bba59d92716

**Issue found: the declared `n_lines` axis is ignored and the default target
count disagrees with every canonical input.** With seed 11 and sample index 7,
`n_lines=1` and `n_lines=4` produce byte-identical grids; each has exactly two
vertical color-1 components of length five. All five canonical inputs contain
exactly three qualifying length-five components. This means override acceptance
can pass while the advertised factor is not learnable or controllable.

**Possible shortcut:** “mark the center of every five-cell vertical window”
rather than “mark the middle of an exact length-five component.” Default
examples contain only exact length-five targets plus length-two/three vertical
decoys. None contains a length-six or branched vertical component. The held-out
canonical input does contain a vertical length-six component (column 7), which
the true rule leaves unchanged, so the missing negative is consequential.

Reproducer and normalized component signatures are retained in
`checks/audit_probe.json`.
